title: Ribes diacanthum Pall modulates bile acid homeostasis and oxidative stress in cholestatic mice by activating the SIRT1/FXR and Keap1/Nrf2 signaling pathways.
authors: Bayoude, Alamusi; Zhang, Jiaxin; Shen, Yuanjiang; Tilyek, Akhtolkhyn; Chai, Chengzhi
one_liner_zh: 该文研究植物提取物对胆汁淤积小鼠的保肝作用，涉及SIRT1/FXR和Keap1/Nrf2通路及分子对接，但核心是药物机制而非蛋白质-DNA互作建模，仅分子对接为边缘方法，与TF-DNA课题关系微弱。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Cholestatic liver injury (CLI) is a pathophysiological syndrome characterized by the accumulation of bile acids (BAs), which leads to significant hepatic dysfunction. This condition is frequently associated with disturbances in BAs homeostasis and the induction of oxidative stress. Ribes diacanthum Pall (RDP), a conventional folk medicinal plant, has been employed in Mongolia, the Inner Mongolia region of China, and other areas for the remediation of hepatic disorders. However, the specific mechanism and chemical composition by which RDP exerts its effects remain unknown. AIM OF THE STUDY: The aim of this research was to assess the protective impact of RDP on CLI and probe into the underlying mechanism and pinpoint the active constituents of RDP. MATERIALS AND METHODS: For this study, a CLI mouse model induced via bile duct ligation (BDL) was used to investigate the hepatoprotective effect of RDP. Mice were administered low, medium, or high doses of RDP for 6 consecutive days, beginning 3 days prior to BDL induction. Subsequently, serum biochemical parameters, hepatic histopathology, and cholestatic markers were analyzed. An HPLC-QTOF-MS/MS analysis was also conducted to identify the prototype constituents in RDP. Furthermore, component-directed network pharmacology was utilized to identify the active constituents, central targets, and signaling cascades of RDP. Eventually, quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) and Western blotting were adopted to confirm the associated antioxidant enzymes, BAs transporters, and metabolic enzymes. Molecular docking was applied to forecast the binding affinity between the components and core targets. RESULTS: RDP effectively ameliorated the pathological liver damage and cholestasis in BDL-induced CLI mice. Moreover, 43 components within RDP were identified through HPLC-QTOF-MS/MS analysis. Altogether 106 potential targets were detected, and the high-affinity targets, namely Keap1 and SIRT1, were located through the PPI network. The results of GO and KEGG analysis indicated that the reaction to oxidative stress and BAs homeostasis are significantly associated with the RDP treatment of CLI. In the in vivo experimental study, the findings revealed that RDP alleviated the BDL-induced oxidative damage. Simultaneously, RDP augmented the expressions of BAs efflux transporters and the metabolic enzymes in liver tissues, thus promoting BAs excretion and metabolism in cholestatic rodents. Mechanically, RDP attenuated hepatic oxidative stress and the accumulation of BAs, protecting the liver from BDL-induced cholestasis via the Keap1/Nrf2 and SIRT1/FXR signaling axis. The molecular docking result indicated that bolusanthol C and 3,6,3',4'-tetrahydroxyflavone possess a superior binding affinity to the two core targets (Keap1, SIRT1). CONCLUSION: These results suggest that RDP ameliorate CLI by regulating BAs homeostasis and alleviating oxidative stress through the SIRT1/FXR and Keap1/Nrf2 signaling pathways, presenting a novel therapeutic strategy for cholestasis. Additionally, bolusanthol C and 3,6,3',4'-tetrahydroxyflavone may function as key pharmacological agents in RDP, responsible for its protective effects against CLI.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：胆汁淤积性肝损伤（CLI）是一种以胆汁酸（BAs）蓄积为特征的病理生理综合征，导致显著的肝功能障碍。该病症常与胆汁酸稳态紊乱及氧化应激诱导相关。刺李（Ribes diacanthum Pall，RDP）是一种传统民间药用植物，在蒙古、中国内蒙古地区及其他区域被用于治疗肝脏疾病。然而，RDP发挥其作用的具体机制和化学成分仍不明确。研究目的：本研究旨在评估RDP对CLI的保护作用，探讨其潜在机制，并确定RDP的活性成分。材料与方法：本研究采用胆管结扎（BDL）诱导的CLI小鼠模型，以探究RDP的肝保护作用。小鼠在BDL诱导前3天开始，连续6天给予低、中或高剂量的RDP。随后，分析血清生化参数、肝组织病理学及胆汁淤积标志物。同时，采用HPLC-QTOF-MS/MS分析鉴定RDP中的原型成分。此外，利用成分导向的网络药理学识别RDP的活性成分、核心靶点及信号级联。最终，采用实时定量聚合酶链反应（qRT-PCR）和Western blotting验证相关的抗氧化酶、胆汁酸转运体及代谢酶。应用分子对接预测成分与核心靶点之间的结合亲和力。结果：RDP有效改善了BDL诱导的CLI小鼠的病理肝损伤和胆汁淤积。此外，通过HPLC-QTOF-MS/MS分析鉴定出RDP中的43种成分。共检测到106个潜在靶点，并通过PPI网络定位了高亲和力靶点，即Keap1和SIRT1。GO和KEGG分析结果表明，氧化应激反应和胆汁酸稳态与RDP治疗CLI显著相关。在体内实验研究中，结果显示RDP减轻了BDL诱导的氧化损伤。同时，RDP增强了肝组织中胆汁酸外排转运体和代谢酶的表达，从而促进胆汁淤积啮齿动物的胆汁酸排泄和代谢。机制上，RDP通过Keap1/Nrf2和SIRT1/FXR信号轴减轻肝氧化应激和胆汁酸蓄积，保护肝脏免受BDL诱导的胆汁淤积。分子对接结果表明，bolusanthol C和3,6,3',4'-四羟基黄酮对两个核心靶点（Keap1、SIRT1）具有优越的结合亲和力。结论：这些结果表明，RDP通过SIRT1/FXR和Keap1/Nrf2信号通路调节胆汁酸稳态并减轻氧化应激，从而改善CLI，为胆汁淤积提供了新的治疗策略。此外，bolusanthol C和3,6,3',4'-四羟基黄酮可能作为RDP中的关键药理活性成分，负责其对CLI的保护作用。
